title: Establish synthetic Fleet/provider performance baseline
body:
## Outcome
Deliver an opt-in reproducible benchmark harness and first synthetic baseline for existing Fleet resolver/broker and provider paths. This measures current behavior; it does not assert BWS is slow or change production resolution. No timings are known yet.

## Current repository evidence
At the inspected baseline, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` resolves through broker then BWS CLI fallback; fallback lists then gets by native ID. `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs` refreshes through BWS CLI, list plus per-item get with bounded 8-way concurrency, and has a memory cache/singleflight path. `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs` exposes only get/list. `fleet-secrets` has no cache or provider SDK dependency. Record the exact commit and actual versions in the report.

## Scope and boundaries
Build deterministic fake-provider harness first. Add optional adapters only for explicitly isolated synthetic test scopes: broker, direct BWS CLI, official Rust SDK if verified compatible, OP CLI, fnox CLI/client, and local SOPS/age. `bw` Password Manager is a separate, approval-gated comparison; never infer authorization from BWS. Writes only against disposable isolated fixtures after explicit authorization. No production/personal vault reads or writes, no real credential values, no mutation of current resolver semantics. Do not emit secret values or secret-bearing stderr.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Benchmark matrix covers cold/warm process and auth; sequential and concurrent 1/10/100+ synthetic reads; batch where supported; first/full paginated list; cache hit/miss; auth overhead; safe create/update/read-back only in disposable store; errors/throttling and recovery.
2. Report p50/p95/p99, sample count, throughput, success/error/timeout/throttle rate, bytes, CPU, peak/RSS memory, process count/startup, token/session churn, observed cache age, exact versions and execution host. Separate network RTT, startup/auth, provider, serialization and cache components where observable. Include laptop and actual agent host when available; provide a 24h low-concurrency soak plan/result before making systemic latency claims.
3. Publish the matrix, raw anonymized timings and repeat command; no numeric pass threshold until baseline is reviewed and targets agreed. Oracle: deterministic fake-provider trace validates case labels/errors; independently recompute quantiles from captured synthetic timings and verify against harness output.
4. A synthetic secret canary must be absent from stdout/stderr, JSON, logs, telemetry and errors.

## Negative tests
Refuse production-designated scopes by default; malformed/partial page, 403, 429, timeout, invalid JSON, absent provider, SDK unsupported, stale cache and read-after-write mismatch are distinct outcomes and never count as deletion. Verify empty secret behavior explicitly without leaking values. A failed provider or unavailable account is labeled unavailable, not a benchmarked absence.

## Dependencies / safe environment
Harness itself has no live-provider dependency. Live-provider comparison requires explicit authorization for a disposable vault/project, scoped credentials, and documented cleanup; otherwise report it unavailable and retain synthetic results. Keep requirement IDs and output linked from #9160.

## Rollback and lifecycle
Opt-in command/feature; no change to existing `get/list`. Disable/remove optional live adapters without impacting broker path. Revert benchmark code without touching secrets. Do not log or commit credentials, vault contents, or production identifiers.

title: Specify per-secret freshness, invalidation and singleflight contract
body:
## Outcome
Define and enforce Fleet's read freshness/invalidation contract, correcting the known stale-after-rotation risk (#6767) without adding a new cache tier. Consumers can distinguish authoritative live values from cached and stale-approved values; outages are not deletions.

## Current repository evidence
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` explicitly stores no cache and uses redacted `SecretValue`; broker source `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs` has fetched-at metadata, TTL, per-key singleflight and partial refresh behavior. Successful individual fetches install; failed fetches retain prior value/age; full-list authority governs removals. Thus age is known, but retaining a prior value does not prove freshness. Preserve partial-list protection.

## Scope and boundaries
Deliver a versioned design/API contract plus implementation/tests for scoped cache identity, provenance/fetched-at, per-secret classification/max age, provider revision where available, write/rotation/revocation invalidation, singleflight and stale response policy. Keep provider selection policy-driven. Do not add persistent cache, sync/reconcile writer, or alter CLI legacy behavior silently. Root/lease/dynamic/revocable values fail closed by default absent reviewed explicit exception. Offline snapshot never authorizes a write or reconciliation.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Cache key includes canonical logical ID and provider/account/project/vault/profile scope; tests prove same name in different scope never aliases.
2. A successful Fleet-mediated update/rotation/revocation invalidates the exact identity and native IDs before reporting success; failed write/readback cannot label the old copy authoritative. External updates are handled through verified event/revision or finite class-specific TTL and explicit refresh.
3. Model-based tests generate cache hit/miss, concurrent callers, rotation, revoke, expiration, provider outage/403, incomplete listing, refresh failure and recovery using fake clock/provider. Invariants: one same-key concurrent miss creates one upstream request; distinct keys proceed; failed refresh does not advance fetched-at; outage/403/partial page never means absent/deleted; revoked or over-age secrets are never served; allowed stale value is explicitly marked and bounded. Oracle is a reference state machine compared against observed fake-provider traces.
4. Status/result metadata reports provider/source, age, cache state and freshness decision without secret value. Errors preserve absent vs inaccessible vs unavailable vs unsupported.

## Negative tests
Stale value after revocation, scope collision, truncated inventory, 403-as-delete, concurrent rotation/read race, failed write/read-back, backward clock, singleflight waiter timeout/cancellation, failed provider refresh, conflict between replicas, and over-max-age fallback all must fail closed per policy. Ensure errors, Debug and logs do not contain value.

## Dependencies / safe environment
No live provider required; use synthetic fixture and fake clock. Review #6767 behavior and coordinate response/API version with existing broker consumers. No production rotation or vault reconciliation.

## Rollback and lifecycle
Add versioned response/policy support and preserve legacy behavior until callers migrate. Kill switch disables fallback/cache serving rather than permitting longer stale use. Rollback must not restore unbounded stale reads. Record per-secret policy defaults and migration.

title: Prototype and decide optional fnox daemon-cache adapter
body:
## Outcome
Build a bounded synthetic prototype and publish go/no-go decision for fnox as an optional read accelerator. Compare fnox CLI, `fnox exec`, published Rust `fnox-client` against the existing Fleet broker/cache. Do not make Fleet's API depend on fnox or assume its daemon grants freshness.

## Current evidence
`fnox-client` docs.rs 1.48.0 (published 2026-11-09) documents `Client::resolve_env`, read-only resolution from an already-running daemon, no provider dependency, no daemon start/store/provider fetch; on miss caller runs CLI. Its wire protocol internals evolve with protocol. fnox daemon docs say in-memory per-user IPC and explicit refresh/clear; it does not know when provider values change. Provider docs show BWS CLI provider can write via fnox but OP/BW human-vault adapters are read-only. Fleet workspace MSRV is Rust 1.85 (`pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml`); exact fnox-client MSRV and dependency compatibility remain to be verified.

## Scope and boundaries
Only use public `fnox-client` API behind optional feature, no private wire protocol; try a bounded allowlist of requested secret keys. Handle hit/miss/disabled/daemon unavailable separately and fallback only according to PERF-02 freshness policy. No broad env dump, provider write, sync/reconcile, root key, live vault, or mandatory fnox install. Assess CLI boundary and reject integration if dependency/MSRV/security/maintenance fails.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Pin exact fnox-client and binary versions; build with Fleet's declared MSRV/toolchain and inspect dependency graph/features/platforms. If not compatible, document verified blocker.
2. Synthetic tests cover daemon hit, cache miss, disabled, absent daemon, wrong wire version, timeout, different config/profile/environment, refresh/clear and malformed result. On miss use Fleet resolver; never interpret miss as missing secret.
3. Benchmark freshness-equivalent paths using PERF-01 measurements; report p50/p95/p99, RSS, startup/process count, cache age, errors and environment. Promote only if p95/p99 improvement for observed workload is materially useful against corrected Fleet path, with no stale/revoked violations and agreed target after baseline. Oracle: synthetic known-value comparison plus call trace establishes no hidden provider I/O and correct fallback; no invented timings.
4. Decision record chooses integrate / CLI-only / reject and documents API stability, memory, same-user threat, maintenance, MSRV and fallback. No measured benefit means no dependency.

## Negative tests
Revoked/rotated secret remains stale in daemon; max-age denial wins over cache hit. Miss/disabled not-found confusion; environment/config mismatch; unsupported wire cannot panic or silently resolve stale value. Canary never appears in argv, logs, errors, or benchmark report. fnox `set`/provider writes are not used.

## Dependencies / safe environment
Requires PERF-01 baseline and PERF-02 freshness API. Synthetic local provider fixtures only; any separate isolated live vault requires explicit approval.

## Rollback and lifecycle
Optional feature and kill switch; fallback preserves Fleet broker/resolver and policy. Remove optional dependency cleanly if unsupported or no benefit. Document supported pinned versions and re-evaluation trigger; no change to deployed daemon or live fnox cache.

title: Add scoped SOPS/age deployment adapter and offline recovery proof
body:
## Outcome
Implement an opt-in Fleet deployment-secret adapter using existing SOPS/age formats and NixOS sops-nix provisioning patterns, with synthetic offline restore, recipient rotation and Nix-store non-disclosure proof. This does not authorize live export or change repository deployment configuration by default.

## Current repository/source evidence
Intake `note.md` says sops-nix patterns already exist in NixOS provisioning but Fleet has no SOPS provider API. Primary SOPS, age and sops-nix docs describe encrypted structured files, multiple age recipients and activation-time runtime secret files with ownership/modes. Age private identities and plaintext must not enter Git or Nix store; exact Fleet Nix key locations/persistence must be inspected by implementation owner.

## Scope and boundaries
Use SOPS/age tools/format, do not implement crypto or create another encrypted format. Synthetic deployment-only values first. Require explicit scope/recipient authorization; no general export of OP/BWS, no root private-key default, no production values, no secret evaluation/interpolation into Nix derivations. Keep age identities out of repo, derivations, store, image, logs and agent prompts; provision runtime identity out of band. Flux/Kubernetes/etcd work remains separate.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Encrypt/decrypt structured and binary synthetic fixture; verify ciphertext recipient metadata and manifest. Prove selected identity decrypts and unselected recipient cannot.
2. Add/rekey recipient; test current ciphertext with new recipient; document old Git ciphertext remains decryptable by removed recipient and require underlying secret rotation if access revocation is required. Test overlap, lost host, disconnected recovery identity and rebuild/bootstrap.
3. sops-nix activation emits expected runtime file owner/mode atomically; clean derivation/store closure, build logs and outputs contain no plaintext canary or private identity. Oracle: independent `sops -d`/age decrypt comparison against synthetic expected bytes plus filesystem permission check and recursive store scan.
4. Manifest-only/dry-run reports metadata and destination only; explicit approved write gate required for installation; restore procedure succeeds offline from separate recovery identity.

## Negative tests
Wrong/missing identity, unauthorized scope/recipient, corrupt ciphertext, traversal/symlink path, partial output, plaintext accidentally interpolated into Nix expression/store/log, recipient removed but stale Git copy, attempted root export and unavailable recovery key all produce safe failure; never plaintext fallback.

## Dependencies / safe environment
Requires PERF-02 classification/freshness policy and owner review of existing NixOS config paths. Synthetic test keys/fixtures only; production use stays approval-blocked.

## Rollback and lifecycle
Opt-in feature; restore prior ciphertext only when its recipient remains authorized. Re-key/rollback guidance must distinguish restoring config from revoking access to historical ciphertext. No modification of live NixOS or deployment secrets in this issue absent additional explicit approval.

title: Review SecureStore format for optional import/export only
body:
## Outcome
Deliver a bounded comparative assessment of NeoSmart SecureStore against age/SOPS and a go/no-go on disposable import/export adapter. This is not adoption, migration, a production cache, or a new default encrypted format.

## Current evidence
`securestore-rs` docs.rs 0.100.3 and upstream README show a Rust `SecretsManager` API and portable v3 JSON format. Upstream format documentation specifies AES-128-CBC, HMAC-SHA1 and PBKDF2-SHA1 (256,000 iterations); Rust crate offers OpenSSL or Rust implementation feature. Direct API is attractive, but the primary docs do not prove independent audit, safe concurrent updates, or long-term maintenance. Existing SOPS/age is already used for NixOS deployment.

## Scope and boundaries
Inspect exact pinned source, release/maintenance policy, dependencies/MSRV, KDF limits, MAC coverage/order, metadata authentication, downgrade/rollback, key custody, atomic save and multiprocess concurrency, recovery, format evolution, interop with .NET implementation. Use synthetic vectors only. Do not store production values, create Fleet dependency, change Cargo workspace or generate new persistent format.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Evidence matrix cites source paths/versions for every crypto/API/lifecycle claim and labels unknowns; independent reviewer performs crypto design review before any deployment-use recommendation.
2. Disposable prototype round-trips synthetic values using official Rust and .NET implementations where practical. Test wrong key, tamper every file component, truncation, old/new format handling, rollback, parallel writer and crash during save; inspect whether updates are atomic/lost. Oracle: known synthetic plaintext bytes, cross-implementation byte/value equality, and expected authenticated failure under mutations.
3. Compare required capabilities against SOPS/age: multi-recipient distribution/recovery, recipient removal/rekey, Nix integration, history/rollback behavior, runtime dependencies, memory/security and maintenance. Final record explicitly chooses reject / optional read-only import-export, with reasons; default remains SOPS/age absent a material unmet requirement.

## Negative tests
Do not claim AES-128-CBC/HMAC-SHA1 is practically broken based solely on primitives; do not claim secure based only on successful roundtrip. Reject unauthenticated/tampered metadata, unsupported/downgrade version, excessive KDF/input resource use, wrong key and concurrent lost update; no secret appears in logs or retained fixture.

## Dependencies / safe environment
No runtime dependency. Pinned upstream source and qualified security reviewer required for a deployment-use recommendation.

## Rollback and lifecycle
Prototype is disposable and has no production footprint. If no-go, remove adapter prototype and keep a tested read-only export path only if separately justified. Any later adoption requires a new explicit design, migration and recovery issue; no mutation/rotation of live stores here.
